title: Soupe a l'Oignon Gratinee
subtitle: French onion soup with a Gruyere crouton lid
excerpt: Slowly caramelised onions in beef stock, topped with toasted bread and melted Gruyere. The lid should be golden and bubbling before it leaves the oven.
sourceNotes: Parisian bistro classic. Long, slow onion caramelisation is the whole foundation of the dish.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the soup base without bread or cheese. Reheat, toast fresh bread, and grill with cheese to finish.
recipe.batchNotes: The soup base scales well. Make a large batch and freeze in portions; finish each bowl individually.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the soup base up to 3 days ahead. Reheat and grill the crouton topping just before serving.

content.text: The onions need at least 45 minutes over low heat to turn deep gold. Rush this step and the soup is flat. The bread lid should float on the surface and be completely covered by cheese before it goes under the grill.

items.prepNote: about 6 large, thinly sliced into half-moons

content.text: Melt the butter and oil in the large saucepan over low heat. Add the onions and a pinch of salt. Stir well to coat.
Cook the onions over low heat for 45 to 55 minutes, stirring every 5 to 10 minutes. They should turn deep golden brown throughout.
Scatter the flour over the onions and stir for 2 minutes. Pour in the wine and let it bubble for 2 minutes.
Add the hot stock, bay leaves, and thyme. Simmer for 20 minutes. Remove the bay and thyme. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat the grill to high. Ladle the hot soup into the oven-safe bowls. Set them on a baking tray.
Place a slice of toasted bread on each bowl. Cover completely with grated Gruyere.
Grill for 4 to 5 minutes until the cheese is bubbling and patched with brown. Serve immediately.

items.symptom: The onions are golden in patches but still pale overall.
items.cause: The heat was too high and they coloured unevenly.
items.fix: Lower the heat and keep cooking. Scrape any dark bits from the base as you stir.

items.symptom: The soup tastes thin or sweet rather than savoury.
items.cause: The stock was weak or the onions were not cooked long enough.
items.fix: Simmer the soup uncovered for 10 more minutes to concentrate, or add a little more stock.

items.symptom: The cheese topping slides off the bread.
items.cause: The bread was not toasted first or the cheese was applied too thinly.
items.fix: Toast the bread firmly before floating it on the soup. Pile the cheese on thickly.
